nodes.label: pseudonymise_user privilege-escalation fix
nodes.rationale: Slice 0.3 DDL as drafted was SECURITY DEFINER + GRANT EXECUTE TO authenticated, letting any logged-in user erase anyone via PostgREST RPC. Fixed design inlines an eventar_staff + status='active' check inside the function, raises insufficient_privilege, and writes a user_pseudonymised audit event in the same transaction.

nodes.label: Audit hash chain race + ordering fix
nodes.rationale: As drafted, no advisory lock in the trigger and (created_at, uuid_v4) ordering was non-deterministic because identity nextval fires before BEFORE-triggers. Fixed design: chain_seq bigint identity column overridden by the trigger via nextval() after acquiring pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('audit_events_chain')); ordering by chain_seq only. Convention: audit insert is the last statement before commit.

nodes.label: Lookup miss-rate signal (replaces RLS-deny-counter)
nodes.rationale: 'RLS deny counter' signal can never fire because RLS on SELECT filters silently. Replaced by lookup miss-rate: fraction of parameterised lookups per session returning empty/404; flag at >60% over 100 requests in 10 min.

nodes.label: Abuse-control design — measurement vs inference
nodes.rationale: Automation is safe when the trigger is a measurement; dangerous when it is an inference. Measurements can auto-act (rate limits, Turnstile, OTP failure bursts); inferences (behavioural signals — cadence, endpoint traversal, lookup miss-rate, endpoint diversity) produce flags only, forever.

nodes.label: Sprint 2 Finding 1 — audit enforcement must be a DB-function shape
nodes.rationale: Every PostgREST RPC executes as its own transaction; an application-layer wrapper calling write_audit_event after a mutation runs the audit write in a separate transaction, violating audit-insert-last. Audited mutations must be SECURITY DEFINER database functions ending with the audit write — pseudonymise_user is the canonical shape. write_audit_event EXECUTE grant revoked from authenticated.

nodes.label: Sprint 2 Finding 2 — Turnstile-deferral window residual risk
nodes.rationale: During the Turnstile deferral window, unauthenticated endpoints have flat per-IP rate limits only — no escalating block, no bot challenge, no strike ladder. A persistent attacker can hammer /login and /otp/* at just-under-rate-limit indefinitely. Acceptable only while the platform is not publicly exposed; public exposure gates on Turnstile provisioning.
